The six Fātiḥa overlay ayat add worship, guidance, mercy, judgment, and paths, but no water trigger. The hydraulic network therefore does not materially change the focus reading.

17:4 explicitly places a decree, corruption, and domineering elevation immediately before the focus threat and dispatch. The causal link from that breach to the counterforce is an inference, so it remains qualified; every supplied trace branch and role is retained.

The focus ordinal is followed by restoration in 17:6, a later promised entry in 17:7, and the reciprocal return condition in 17:8. These distinct context events support the HFT's reversible-cycle reading without turning the two promises into the same event.

The general time passage does not identify the promise's date, so the measured-versus-hasty relation remains qualified; all four candidate branches and their trace roles are retained.

17:13 attaches a written record to each person, and 17:15 keeps burdens nontransferable and punishment after a messenger. Their shared dispatch root returns through the focus sending, supporting a chapter-level accountability frame while leaving episode-specific mechanics open.

The nominated B007 branch names a person by attachment to land or home, while the actual focus carrier is the dwellings themselves; that branch is excluded and the dwelling-to-city core is retained through the focus B002 branch.

findings.title: Penetration Through the Dwellings
findings.claim: The focus stages the first promised event as a threat made concrete by dispatch: a forceful group moves through the gaps of inhabited space. The later sanctuary entry and dismantling in 17:7 extend that spatial incursion, while 17:6 and 17:8 place it within reversal and conditional return.
findings.mechanism: The focus noun waʿd gains threat force from the named severe might and the agents' action; baʿathnā supplies directed sending, and jāsū plus khilāl al-diyār supplies movement through domestic interstices. In 17:7, entry into the sanctuary is explicitly compared with an earlier entry, then followed by dismantling. The turn in 17:6 and reciprocal return in 17:8 add a bounded consequence sequence to the physical route.
findings.reader_payoff: The dwellings become the route and target of an incursion rather than scenery, and the later matched entry makes its spatial pattern perceptible across the pericope.
findings.containment: The packet supports severe force, movement through dwellings, a later compared entry, restoration, and conditional return. This does not identify the historical agents, treat both entries as the same event, or make the promised violence a free-standing moral judgment.

epistemic.reason: Trusted channel supports and the focus surface agree on threat, dispatch, force, gaps, and the matched entry; the broader reversal and return are supplied as contextual evidence.

findings.title: Measured Promise Timing
findings.claim: The focus promise remains an appointed future event, and the sequence around 17:11-12 lets its arrival be heard against human haste as part of measured, countable time.

epistemic.reason: The focus branches are present in the packet and the context words are exact-coordinate HFT traces; their linkage to this particular promise is inferred from a legacy-unbound response.

findings.title: Notice, Record, and Enforcement
findings.claim: The focus dispatch can be read within a chapter-level accountability frame: personal records and nontransferable burdens accompany the rule that punishment follows a messenger, qualifying the force as consequence under individual accounting.
findings.mechanism: The focus baʿathnā is the carrier of directed dispatch. In 17:13 each person's record is attached and made visible; in 17:15 burdens are not transferred and punishment is not sent before a messenger. These distinct contextual relations meet the focus dispatch and its plural agents, changing an undifferentiated collective-penalty reading into a bounded consequence within notice and individual accountability.
findings.reader_payoff: The plural incursion remains public, while the surrounding passage keeps each person's record and responsibility in view.
findings.containment: The HFT calls the messenger dispatch parallel to, but distinct from, the focus dispatch. This does not claim that the armed agents are messengers, that the focus episode's timing is fully specified by 17:15, or that the later general rule narrates the episode's exact mechanics.

epistemic.reason: The context coordinates and focus return agree with the supplied surface, but the notice-record-enforcement sequence is the attributed HFT inference and its source identity is unbound.

findings.title: Instrumentality and Evaluation
findings.claim: The focus calls the agents God's servants and says they were sent; the later distinction between immediate and hereafter aims, with provision extended to both, permits a bounded distinction between commissioned instrumentality and ultimate moral evaluation.
findings.mechanism: The focus servant and dispatch phrases carry belonging and assigned action. In 17:18-20, different aims are named and both groups receive worldly provision; this independent contrast shows that worldly effectiveness or gift is not itself a complete moral verdict. Read back through the focus words, deployment establishes a function without settling every aspect of the agents' standing.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can register the force of the commission without treating its effectiveness alone as a complete appraisal of its bearers.
findings.containment: The later provision passage does not identify the focus agents as either group and does not prove that they lack approval. The connection row for 17:20 explicitly resists using it to explain the promise or incursion; this finding uses it only to bound the inference about evaluation.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus and 17:20 HFT traces are supplied, while the two aims are also directly present in the inline 17:18-19 context. The role remains an attributed contextual qualification.
